hindi: अब इसलिए हम विरेचन-कल्प की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the preparations of purgation (virecana-kalpa).

lines_deva: विरेचनद्रव्याणां मूलेषु त्रिवृत्त्वक्षु तिल्वकः क्षीरेषु स्नुही फलेषु हरीलकी प्रधानानि
lines_iast: virecanadravyāṇāṃ mūleṣu trivṛttvakṣu tilvakaḥ kṣīreṣu snuhī phaleṣu harīlakī pradhānāni

words.gloss: tilvaka (disputed: Symplocos racemosa, i.e. lodhra, or Wendlandia exserta)
snuhī (Euphorbia neriifolia, a milky-sap spurge; standard)

hindi: विरेचन द्रव्यों में प्रधान ये हैं: मूलों में त्रिवृत् यानी निसोथ, त्वचाओं में तिल्वक, दूधों में स्नुही यानी सेहुंड और फलों में हरीतकी यानी हरड़।
english: Among purgation substances the foremost are: among roots, trivṛt (turpeth); among barks, tilvaka; among milks, snuhī (a spurge); among fruits, harītakī (chebulic myrobalan).

text_flags.why: possible: la for ta (harītakī is the usual drug name)

notes: kṣīra rendered literally as 'milk' (it could also mean a milky sap); the text only says 'among milks'. Distribution: each locative names the class and the nominative names the foremost item. Identification confidence: trivṛt = Operculina turpethum (standard); snuhī = Euphorbia neriifolia (standard); harītakī = Terminalia chebula (standard); tilvaka is disputed (Symplocos racemosa, the plant called lodhra, and Wendlandia exserta are both proposed), so no Hindi common name is given for it.

lines_deva: त्रिवृतायाः खलु द्विविधं मूलमरुणं श्यामं च
lines_iast: trivṛtāyāḥ khalu dvividhaṃ mūlamaruṇaṃ śyāmaṃ ca

words.gloss: of trivṛtā (= trivṛt, turpeth; see line 05.02.2)

hindi: त्रिवृत् यानी निसोथ का मूल निश्चय ही दो प्रकार का है: लालिमायुक्त और श्याम।
english: Indeed, the root of trivṛt (turpeth) is of two kinds: reddish and dark.
notes: aruṇa 'reddish' and śyāma 'dark' are colour words; the text names them as the two kinds.

lines_deva: तत्रारुणं कषायमधुरं विपाके कटुकं रूक्षं श्लेष्मपित्तहरं कल्पनाविशेषात्पुनः सर्वव्याधिशमनं सुखविरेचनत्वाच्छिशुस्थविरसुकुमारमृदुकोष्ठेषु प्रशस्तं त्रिवृच्छब्दवाच्यं च
lines_iast: tatrāruṇaṃ kaṣāyamadhuraṃ vipāke kaṭukaṃ rūkṣaṃ śleṣmapittaharaṃ kalpanāviśeṣātpunaḥ sarvavyādhiśamanaṃ sukhavirecanatvācchiśusthavirasukumāramṛdukoṣṭheṣu praśastaṃ trivṛcchabdavācyaṃ ca

words.gloss: in the young, aged, delicate and soft-koṣṭha

hindi: उन दोनों में लालिमायुक्त मूल कसैला और मधुर है, विपाक में कटु है, रूक्ष है और कफ तथा पित्त को हरने वाला है; फिर विशेष विधि से तैयार करने पर सब व्याधियों को शान्त करने वाला है; सुखपूर्वक विरेचन कराने के कारण शिशु, वृद्ध, सुकुमार और मृदु कोष्ठ वालों में प्रशस्त है; और वह 'त्रिवृत्' शब्द से कहा जाता है।
english: Of these two, the reddish one is astringent and sweet, pungent in vipāka (the post-digestive stage), dry, and removes Kapha (śleṣman) and Pitta; moreover, through a particular preparation it pacifies all ailments; because it purges easily, it is recommended in the young, the aged, the delicate and those whose koṣṭha (abdomen, bowel) is soft; and it is what is denoted by the word trivṛt.
notes:
kaṣāya here is the taste 'astringent' (not 'decoction'; cf. GLOSSARY OPEN item kaṣāya/kvātha/niryūha). śleṣman = Kapha (synonym). The long compound śiśu-sthavira-sukumāra-mṛdu-koṣṭheṣu may be read as persons (the young, the aged, the delicate) plus 'those of soft koṣṭha', or all four as qualifying koṣṭha; rendered as persons. 'kalpanā-viśeṣāt' = from a particular manner of preparation, not specified here. vipāka, koṣṭha kept with a gloss.
OPEN (05.02.4) [minor] english / koṣṭha (abdomen, bowel): "bowel" is an interpretive narrowing of koṣṭha (lit. inner chamber, belly). Not a draft-only error; see glossary_suggestions. Suggested: koṣṭha (belly, abdominal interior)

lines_deva: इतरदपि तस्माद्गुणैः किंचिद्धीनं तीक्ष्णं कंठहृदयकर्षणं मूर्च्छासंमोहकृदाशु दोषहरत्वाद्वहुदोषक्लेशक्षमक्रूरकोष्ठेषु प्रशस्तं श्यामाशब्दवाच्यं च
lines_iast: itaradapi tasmādguṇaiḥ kiṃciddhīnaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ kaṃṭhahṛdayakarṣaṇaṃ mūrcchāsaṃmohakṛdāśu doṣaharatvādvahudoṣakleśakṣamakrūrakoṣṭheṣu praśastaṃ śyāmāśabdavācyaṃ ca

words.gloss: in those with many doṣas, able to bear distress, with hard koṣṭha

hindi: दूसरा मूल भी उससे गुणों में कुछ हीन है, तीक्ष्ण है, कण्ठ और हृदय को खींचने वाला है, मूर्च्छा और सम्मोह करने वाला है; दोषों को शीघ्र हरने के कारण बहुत दोष वाले, क्लेश सहने में समर्थ और कठोर कोष्ठ वालों में प्रशस्त है; और वह 'श्यामा' शब्द से कहा जाता है।
english: The other one too is somewhat inferior to that in qualities; it is sharp, pulls at the throat and heart, and causes fainting and bewilderment; because it quickly removes the doṣas, it is recommended in those with many doṣas, who can bear distress, and whose koṣṭha (abdomen, bowel) is hard; and it is what is denoted by the word śyāmā.

text_flags.why: possible: va for ba in 'bahu' (the edition confuses ba and va)

notes: āśu 'quickly' may go with mūrcchā-saṃmoha-kṛt or with doṣa-haratvāt; rendered with the latter. krūra-koṣṭha rendered 'hard koṣṭha' (krūra lit. 'cruel, harsh'). The compound bahu-doṣa-kleśa-kṣama-krūra-koṣṭheṣu is read as three descriptions of persons (many doṣas; bearing distress; harsh koṣṭha).

hindi: अब उन दोनों में से जो मूल तिरछा फैला हुआ न हो, गहराई में गया हुआ और चिकना हो, उसे संग्रह करे।
english: Now, of the two, one should collect the root that is not spread out sideways, has gone deep, and is smooth.
notes: āharet rendered 'collect' (lit. 'bring, fetch').

hindi: फिर छाल को सुखाकर भली-भाँति रख ले।
english: Then, having dried the bark, one should keep it properly.

words.gloss: combined with śuṇṭhī (dried ginger, Zingiber officinale; standard) and saindhava (rock salt)

hindi: उस चूर्ण को शुण्ठी यानी सोंठ और सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक से युक्त करके, अम्ल पदार्थों के साथ अथवा मांस-रस के साथ भी, वात के रोगों में पीना चाहिए।
english: In ailments of Vāta one should drink that powder, combined with śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and saindhava (rock salt), with sour things or also with meat juice.
notes: amlaiḥ is left as 'sour things' (the text names no particular sour substances). Alternative: 'with sour (liquids)'.

words.gloss: milk, honey, drākṣā (grape or raisin, Vitis vinifera; standard), ikṣu (sugarcane, Saccharum officinarum; standard), juice of kāśmarya (Gmelina arborea; standard), ghee

hindi: पित्त से उत्पन्न रोगों में, दूध, मधु, द्राक्षा यानी अंगूर या मुनक्का, इक्षु यानी गन्ना, काश्मर्य यानी गम्भारी का स्वरस और घृत मिलाकर, मधुर क्वाथों के साथ तथा शर्करा सहित, उसे पिए।
english: In (ailments) arising from Pitta, (one should drink it) with milk, honey, drākṣā (grape or raisin), ikṣu (sugarcane), the expressed juice of kāśmarya (gmelina), and ghee, with sweet decoctions, and with sugar.

text_flags.why: possible: kāthaiḥ for kvāthaiḥ (decoctions); 'kātha' is not a known word

notes:
The verb 'pibet' is carried over from line 05.02.8 (the sentence continues); the compound kṣīra-...-sarpiḥ is read as a dvandva list of things mixed in. 'pitta-uttheṣu' lit. 'risen from Pitta', noun (roges) supplied. kvātha = decoction (GLOSSARY). GROUPING: line 05.02.9 continues the sentence of line 05.02.8; lines 05.02.8, 05.02.9 and 05.02.10 each give a different Vāta/Pitta/Kapha use of the same powder. As printed, 'sarpiḥ' (n. nom./acc. sg.) cannot itself be instrumental, yet the list is translated with 'with'. Either an instrumental (sarpirbhiḥ) is intended, or the list is one long instrumental compound running on through 'svādu-kvāthaiḥ' (… -svarasa-sarpiḥ-svādu-kvāthaiḥ), the printed space being a spacing slip. Sense unchanged.
OPEN (05.02.9) [minor] text_flags / svādukāthaiḥ -> svādukvāthaiḥ: Suggestion is plausible, but line 05.02.10 also has a kātha-type form (pañcakolakkathair), so the edition may spell kvātha as kātha (काथ) throughout. The flag should say it may be a spelling variant, not only a scan slip. The sense (decoction) is not in doubt. Suggested: append note

words.gloss: with urine, honey, kṣāra (alkali), ariṣṭa (fermented medicinal liquor), juice of pīlu (Salvadora persica; probable), and decoctions of triphalā (the three myrobalans) and of pañcakola (the five-kola group)
mixed through with powder of vyoṣa (the three pungents)

hindi: कफ से उत्पन्न रोगों में, मूत्र, मधु, क्षार यानी खार, अरिष्ट यानी किण्वित औषधीय पेय, पीलु का रस, तथा त्रिफला यानी हरड़, बहेड़ा और आँवला और पंचकोल यानी पीपर, पिपलामूल, चव्य, चित्रक और सोंठ के क्वाथों के साथ, व्योष यानी सोंठ, पीपर और काली मिर्च के चूर्ण में मिलाकर, उसे पिए।
english: In (ailments) born of Kapha, (one should drink it) with urine, honey, alkali (kṣāra), ariṣṭa (fermented medicinal liquor), pīlu juice, and the decoctions of triphalā (the three myrobalans) and of pañcakola (the five-kola group), mixed through with vyoṣa (the three pungents) powder.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kkatha' for kvātha (decoction)
possible: yoṣa for vyoṣa (v dropped; 'yoṣa' = woman makes no sense here, and unit 11 has vyoṣa)

notes: 'pibet' carried over from line 05.02.8. Technical names kept: kṣāra (alkali), ariṣṭa, pīlu, triphalā (three fruits), pañcakola (five kola), vyoṣa (drug-group name). Which urine is not stated. The dvandva of 'kvāthaiḥ' may be read so that only the last two are decoctions; rendered as above. GROUPING: continues the sentence of lines 05.02.8-9. The printed 'kkathair' may stand for kāthair (the spelling seen in line 05.02.9, svādukāthaiḥ) or kvāthair; in either case the sense is 'decoctions'. Group members and identifications (each given once for this chunk): triphalā = harītakī, bibhītaka (Terminalia bellirica) and āmalaka (Phyllanthus emblica) (standard). vyoṣa = śuṇṭhī, pippalī (Piper longum) and marica (Piper nigrum) (standard). pañcakola = pippalī, pippalīmūla (root of pippalī), cavya (Piper retrofractum, probable), citraka (Plumbago zeylanica, standard) and śuṇṭhī (standard). pīlu = Salvadora persica (probable; other trees have been proposed). ariṣṭa = a fermented medicinal liquor (standard class). kṣāra = an alkaline preparation, usually from plant ash (standard); which kṣāra is not stated.

lines_deva: एभिरेव च द्रव्यैर्यथास्वं घृतशर्कराक्षोडतवक्षीरीमधुराणि मातुलुंगदाडिमामलककोल्करमर्द्ककपित्थरसतक्राम्लानि सैंधवलवणानि व्योषतीक्ष्णानि विविधवेसवारपूरितानि सहकाररसत्रिजातकनागकेशरकपूरसुरभीणि लेहगुटिकामोदकभक्ष्यभोज्यांन्युपकल्पयेदिति
lines_iast: ebhireva ca dravyairyathāsvaṃ ghṛtaśarkarākṣoḍatavakṣīrīmadhurāṇi mātuluṃgadāḍimāmalakakolkaramardkakapittharasatakrāmlāni saiṃdhavalavaṇāni vyoṣatīkṣṇāni vividhavesavārapūritāni sahakārarasatrijātakanāgakeśarakapūrasurabhīṇi lehaguṭikāmodakabhakṣyabhojyāṃnyupakalpayediti

words.gloss: sweet with ghee, sugar, akṣoḍa (walnut, Juglans regia; standard), tavakṣīrī (disputed: Curcuma angustifolia starch, or bamboo manna)

sour with the juice of mātuluṅga (citron, Citrus medica; standard), dāḍima (pomegranate, Punica granatum; standard), āmalaka (emblic myrobalan, see line 05.02.10), kola (jujube, Ziziphus jujuba; probable), karamardaka (karaunda, Carissa carandas; standard), kapittha (wood-apple, Limonia acidissima; standard), and buttermilk (takra)
filled with various vesavāra (a spiced preparation, traditionally of boned minced meat; probable)

fragrant with sahakāra (mango, Mangifera indica; standard) juice, trijātaka (cinnamon bark, Cinnamomum verum; cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum; bay leaf, Cinnamomum tamala; standard), nāgakeśara (Mesua ferrea stamens; standard), karpūra (camphor, Cinnamomum camphora; standard)

hindi: और इन्हीं द्रव्यों से, अपने-अपने अनुसार, लेह, गुटिका, मोदक, भक्ष्य और भोज्य पदार्थ तैयार करे: जो घृत, शर्करा, अक्षोड यानी अखरोट और तवक्षीरी से मधुर हों; मातुलुंग यानी बिजौरा नींबू, दाडिम यानी अनार, आमलक यानी आँवला, कोल यानी बेर, करमर्दक यानी करौंदा और कपित्थ यानी कैथ के रस तथा तक्र यानी छाछ से अम्ल हों; सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक से लवणयुक्त हों; व्योष यानी सोंठ, पीपर और काली मिर्च से तीक्ष्ण हों; नाना प्रकार के वेसवार से भरे हों; और सहकार यानी आम के रस, त्रिजातक यानी दालचीनी, इलायची और तेजपात, नागकेशर तथा कर्पूर यानी कपूर से सुगन्धित हों; इस प्रकार।
english: And with these very substances, each according to its own, one should prepare lehas (licked preparations), pills, modakas, and bhakṣya and bhojya foods: sweet with ghee, sugar, akṣoḍa (walnut) and tavakṣīrī; sour with the juice of mātuluṅga (citron), dāḍima (pomegranate), āmalaka (emblic myrobalan), kola (jujube), karamardaka (karaunda) and kapittha (wood-apple), and with buttermilk; salty with saindhava (rock salt); sharp with vyoṣa (the three pungents); filled with various vesavāra (a spiced preparation); and fragrant with sahakāra (mango) juice, trijātaka (cinnamon bark, cardamom and bay leaf), nāgakeśara (Ceylon ironwood stamens) and karpūra (camphor); thus.

text_flags.why: possible: vowels and ka dropped in the scan (kola, karamardaka, kapittha)
possible: r dropped (karpūra)
extra anusvāra after bhojyā (ā + ṃ + ny); read bhojyāni upakalpayet

notes: yathāsvam 'each according to its own' (its own property is not specified). kinds of taste named by the compounds: sweet, sour, salty, sharp (tīkṣṇa lit. 'sharp'); the text names no bitter or astringent group. vesavāra: preparation name kept. All drug names kept in the translation; identifications are given beside them in the word glosses with confidence words (tavakṣīrī disputed; kola, vesavāra probable; the rest standard). 'iti' closes the instruction and is rendered 'thus'. The word split of the first compound is uncertain: ghṛta-śarkarā-akṣoḍa-tavakṣīrī-madhurāṇi could also be read as 'ghee, sugar, akṣoḍa, tavakṣīrī, and sweet things'; the parallel with the next compounds (X-amlāni, X-lavaṇāni, X-tīkṣṇāni) favours 'sweet with'. Foods bhakṣya (to be chewed) and bhojya (to be eaten) kept as the two classes.

hindi: और इस विषय में यह है।
english: And in this matter there is this (verse).
notes:
Introductory formula 'bhavati cātra' ('and here there is ...'); it introduces the verses of lines 05.02.13-37. GROUPING: this is a formula unit that introduces the following verse(s); it belongs with line 05.02.13.
OPEN (05.02.12) [minor] notes / GROUPING: Unit 12 is only the lead-in formula "bhavati cātra"; it has no content of its own. Suggest merging it into line 05.02.13 (lead-in line of the first verse), as the draft brief treats such formulas. Suggested: merge 12 into 13

words.gloss: with a decoction of trivṛt paste
combined with honey and trijāta (read as trijātaka: cinnamon bark, cardamom, bay leaf; probable)

hindi: त्रिवृत् के कल्क के क्वाथ से सिद्ध किया हुआ, शर्करा सहित हिम, मधु और त्रिजात यानी दालचीनी, इलायची और तेजपात से मिला हुआ लेह हृदय को प्रिय विरेचन है।
english: A hima (cold preparation), prepared with a decoction of trivṛt paste (kalka), together with sugar, Combined with honey and trijāta (the three aromatics: cinnamon bark, cardamom, bay leaf), the leha (licked preparation) is a heart-pleasing purgative.

text_flags.why: ṭrī for tri (misprint); trijāta (as trijātaka in unit 11) is the drug-group name

notes:
line 05.02.13: kaṣāya here = decoction (GLOSSARY: all 'decoction'; OPEN whether to keep kaṣāya/kvātha/niryūha apart). kalka = paste. trivṛt-kalka-kaṣāya may mean 'decoction made with trivṛt paste' or 'paste and decoction of trivṛt'; rendered as the first. sita 'white' taken as sugar. hima lit. 'cold'; kept with a gloss. GROUPING: lines 05.02.13 and 05.02.14 form one verse and one sentence (hima ... is a lick, a heart-pleasing purgative).
line 05.02.14: hṛdyam lit. 'of/for the heart, agreeable'; kept as 'heart-pleasing'. trijāta = drug-group name, kept. GROUPING: line 05.02.14 completes the verse begun in line 05.02.13.

words.gloss: ajagandhā (disputed: Gynandropsis gynandra or other plants), tavakṣīrī (disputed, see line 05.02.11), vidārī (Pueraria tuberosa, Indian kudzu tuber; probable; Ipomoea digitata is also called vidārī), sugar, trivṛt

hindi: अजगन्धा, तवक्षीरी, विदारी यानी विदारीकन्द, शर्करा और त्रिवृत्, चूर्ण बनाकर मधु और घृत के साथ चाट लेने पर मनुष्य भली-भाँति विरेचित होता है।
english: Ajagandhā, tavakṣīrī, vidārī (Indian kudzu tuber), sugar (śarkarā) and trivṛt, Powdered and licked up with honey and ghee, one is well purged.

text_flags.why: dhyā for bhyā (misprint); instrumental dual of madhu-sarpis

notes:
line 05.02.15: Drug names kept. The list continues into line 05.02.16. GROUPING: lines 05.02.15 and 05.02.16 form one verse and one sentence (these, powdered and licked with honey and ghee, one is well purged).
line 05.02.16: viricyate is impersonal passive; 'one' (a person) supplied.

ENRICHMENT: viḍa as a drug name is probably viḍa-lavaṇa, a prepared (fire-processed) salt (probable; not certain here).
line 05.02.152: The reading of 'viśi' is doubtful; 'in the stool' is only a guess. 'it' (the preparation of the earlier units) is supplied as subject. gulma is kept as a disease name. ENRICHMENT: gulma = abdominal lump or mass (standard); vibandha = obstruction of stool, constipation (standard). The doubtful 'viḍi/viśi' is left unenriched.

words.gloss: cooked with mudga (green gram, Vigna radiata: standard) etc.
dantī (Baliospermum montanum: standard), dravantī (disputed), marica (black pepper, Piper nigrum: standard), svarṇakṣīrī (Argemone mexicana: probable), yavānaka (ajwain, Trachyspermum ammi: probable)

hindi: मुद्ग यानी मूँग आदि के साथ पकाई गई उनकी जड़ों से यूष आदि तैयार करे। दन्ती यानी जंगली जमालगोटा, द्रवन्ती, मरिच यानी काली मिर्च, स्वर्णक्षीरी यानी सम्भवतः सत्यानाशी और यवानक यानी सम्भवतः अजवायन,
english: One should prepare soups (yūṣa) and the like with their roots, cooked with mudga (green gram) and the like. dantī (Baliospermum montanum), dravantī (identity disputed), marica (black pepper), svarṇakṣīrī (prickly poppy, probable) and yavānaka (ajwain, probable),
notes:
line 05.02.153: Construction is loose: 'siddhaiḥ' and 'tanmūlaiḥ' are both instrumental plural; 'cooked with mudga etc.' is taken with 'their roots'. 'their' (tat) has no clear referent. mudga is kept as a name. ENRICHMENT: mudga = green gram, Vigna radiata (standard).
line 05.02.154: All five are kept as drug names. The sentence continues in the next unit. ENRICHMENT: dantī = Baliospermum montanum (standard); dravantī = disputed (several purgative euphorbiaceous plants proposed; left unidentified here); marica = Piper nigrum (standard); svarṇakṣīrī = Argemone mexicana (probable; other plants also proposed); yavānaka = Trachyspermum ammi, ajwain (probable; yavānī). The note 'kept as drug names' above is superseded.

words.gloss: together with śuṇṭhī (dried ginger, Zingiber officinale: standard), agnika (probably citraka, Plumbago zeylanica: probable), pṛthvīka (disputed)

hindi: शुण्ठी यानी सोंठ, अग्निक और पृथ्वीक के साथ, चूर्ण किया हुआ, समान दिनों तक। मूत्र से भावित को घी के साथ पीए, और जीर्ण हो जाने पर तर्पण लेना चाहिए।
english: together with śuṇṭhī (dried ginger), agnika and pṛthvīka (identity disputed), powdered, for equal days. Steeped in urine, one should drink it with ghee; and when it is digested, tarpaṇa (satiation).
notes:
line 05.02.155: 'samavāsarān' (accusative of duration, 'for equal days') is unclear in context; perhaps linked to the steeping in the next unit. Not firmly resolved. śuṇṭhī, agnika, pṛthvīka kept as drug names. ENRICHMENT: śuṇṭhī = dried ginger (standard); agnika = citraka, Plumbago zeylanica (probable; the name also fits other plants); pṛthvīka = disputed (cardamom-type or Nigella proposed). Only the surest words enriched in this low-confidence unit.
line 05.02.156: 'tarpaṇam' has no verb; 'should be taken' supplied in Hindi. What is digested (jīrṇe) is not stated.

lines_iast: sarvadā sarvarogeṣu bāle vṛddhe ca taddhitaṃ

words.gloss: in ill-eating, indigestion, pain in the side, gulma (abdominal lump), spleen (plīha), belly (udara)

hindi: सदा, सभी रोगों में तथा बालक और वृद्ध में वह हितकर है। और दुर्भुक्त, अजीर्ण, पार्श्व की पीड़ा, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, प्लीहा यानी तिल्ली और उदर में।
english: Always, in all ailments and in a child and an old person, that is beneficial. and in ill-eating, indigestion, pain in the side, gulma (abdominal lump), the spleen and the belly (udara).
notes: line 05.02.158: 'plīhodareṣu' is taken as 'spleen' and 'belly' separately; it could also be one term, 'plīhodara'. ENRICHMENT: gulma = abdominal lump (standard); plīha = spleen. If 'plīhodara' is one term it is the enlarged-spleen type of udara disease (probable); the udara = 'belly' decision is kept.

lines_deva: गंडमालासु बाते च पांडुरोगे च शस्यते

words.gloss: in gaṇḍamālā (garland of lumps; scrofula, swollen neck glands: probable)

hindi: गण्डमाला यानी कण्ठमाला में, वात में और पाण्डुरोग यानी रक्ताल्पता में वह प्रशंसित है। आठ पल गुड़ के साथ बीस पथ्या यानी हरड़ हों, एक-एक पल।
english: In gaṇḍamālā (literally 'garland of lumps'; usually equated with scrofula, swelling of the neck glands), in Vāta, and in pāṇḍu-roga (the pale-ailment, usually equated with anaemia), it is commended. To eight palas of jaggery (guḍa), there should be twenty pathyā (chebulic myrobalan), a pala each.

text_flags.why: b/v confusion common in this edition; 'vāta' is the term meant (Vāta)

notes:
line 05.02.159: ENRICHMENT: gaṇḍamālā = scrofula / chain of swellings of the neck glands (probable); pāṇḍu-roga = anaemia (probable, usual equation).
OPEN (05.02.159) [minor] text_flags / bāte: 'b/v confusion common in this edition' is an unverified claim about the edition; also the correction is near-certain (Vāta), so say 'b/v interchange; vāta is the term meant'. words.gloss: of dantī (Baliospermum montanum) and citraka (leadwort, Plumbago zeylanica: standard)
of pippalī (long pepper, Piper longum: standard) and trivṛt (turpeth, Operculina turpethum: standard)

hindi: दन्ती और चित्रक यानी चीता के दो कर्ष, पिप्पली यानी पीपर और त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ के दस। मोदक बनाकर, प्रत्येक दसवें दिन एक।
english: Of dantī and citraka (leadwort), two karṣas; of pippalī (long pepper) and trivṛt (turpeth), ten. Having prepared the balls (modaka), one on every tenth day,
notes:
line 05.02.161: karṣa is a measure. The unit of 'ten' is not stated (presumably karṣas). It is unclear whether 'two karṣas' is for each or both. dantī, citraka, pippalī kept as drug names; trivṛt is literally 'threefold', kept as a drug name. ENRICHMENT: citraka = Plumbago zeylanica (standard); pippalī = Piper longum (standard); trivṛt = Operculina turpethum (standard); dantī = Baliospermum montanum (standard, tagged in line 05.02.154).
line 05.02.162: 'ekam' is taken as 'one' (one ball at a time); the verb comes in the next unit.

hindi: ऊपर से गरम जल पीते हुए, इस विधि से उन सबको खाए। ये परिहार से रहित हों, सब व्याधियों के नाशक।
english: drinking warm water after, one should eat all of them by this method. These would be without avoidances (restrictions), destroyers of all ailments.
notes: line 05.02.164: niṣparihāra: literally 'without avoidance', taken as having nothing to be avoided.

words.gloss: of grahaṇī (a chronic bowel and digestion disorder), pāṇḍu (anaemia), itch, koṭha (urticarial wheals: probable), arśas (haemorrhoids, piles: standard)

hindi: विशेष रूप से ग्रहणी यानी संग्रहणी, पाण्डु यानी रक्ताल्पता, कण्डु यानी खुजली, कोठ यानी शीतपित्त के चकत्ते और अर्श यानी बवासीर के लिए ये हितकर हैं। विरेचन में ये त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ आदि ही सबसे मुख्य नहीं हैं।
english: Especially, they are beneficial for grahaṇī (a chronic bowel and digestion disorder), pāṇḍu (anaemia), itching (kaṇḍu), koṭha (urticarial wheals) and arśas (haemorrhoids, piles). In purging, these trivṛt (turpeth) and the rest are not indeed the most principal.
notes:
line 05.02.165: grahaṇī, koṭha, arśas are kept as the names given. The genitive 'of' is rendered 'for'. ENRICHMENT: grahaṇī = chronic bowel/digestive disorder with loose stools, malabsorption-like (probable); koṭha = urticarial wheals or rash (probable); arśas = haemorrhoids (standard); pāṇḍu = anaemia (probable); kaṇḍu = itching.
line 05.02.166: 'naivaite' = na eva ete; the sense (not the chief ones, or not the only ones) is unclear. Rendered literally; the next unit adds harītakī. Sense check: the negation sits oddly beside the next unit, which prepares harītakī 'also' by the trivṛt method. The printed text is kept; a misprint is possible but no emendation is proposed.

words.gloss: harītakī (= pathyā, chebulic myrobalan, Terminalia chebula)
removing grahaṇī (bowel disorder), pāṇḍu (anaemia), wasting (śoṣa), bewilderment (moha), belly (udara)

hindi: हरीतकी यानी हरड़ को भी त्रिवृत् की विधि से तैयार करे। विशेषतः ग्रहणी यानी संग्रहणी, पाण्डु यानी रक्ताल्पता, शोष यानी सूखकर क्षीण होना, मोह और उदर को दूर करने वाली।
english: One should prepare harītakī (chebulic myrobalan) also by the method of trivṛt. especially removing grahaṇī (bowel disorder), pāṇḍu (anaemia), wasting (śoṣa), bewilderment (moha) and the belly (udara).
notes: line 05.02.168: 'apahām' (feminine) qualifies harītakī of the previous unit. 'udara' is rendered with its plain sense 'belly'; it could also be a named ailment.

words.gloss: together with sindhūttha (rock salt: standard), viḍaṅga (Embelia ribes: standard), utpala (lotus; identity disputed here), nāgara (dried ginger: standard)
of vatsaka (kuṭaja, Holarrhena antidysenterica: standard) etc.

hindi: सिन्धूत्थ यानी सेंधा नमक, विडङ्ग यानी वायविडंग, उत्पल और नागर यानी सोंठ के साथ पथ्या यानी हरड़ को पीए। मूत्र से, अथवा वत्सक यानी कुटज आदि के क्वाथ से, हरीतकी को।
english: One should drink pathyā (chebulic myrobalan) together with sindhūttha (rock salt), viḍaṅga (Embelia ribes), utpala (lotus; identity disputed) and nāgara (dried ginger). With urine, or with a decoction of vatsaka (kuṭaja) and the others, harītakī.

ENRICHMENT: sindhūttha = rock salt, saindhava (standard); viḍaṅga = Embelia ribes (standard); nāgara = dried ginger, same as śuṇṭhī (standard); utpala = disputed (blue lotus / water lily, or Costus speciosus proposed); left unidentified.

words.gloss: powder of pathyā (chebulic myrobalan) and nāgara (dried ginger)

hindi: अथवा पथ्या यानी हरड़ और नागर यानी सोंठ का चूर्ण, कोलिनी के फल से संयुक्त। गुड़ के साथ खाए, और उसके बाद गुनगुना जल पीए।

words.gloss: one with yakṣman (a wasting disease, usually equated with tuberculosis: probable)

hindi: पथ्या यानी हरड़ और त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ से गोलियाँ बनानी चाहिए, शहद और रस से युक्त। माष के परिमाण की वे सूखी गोलियाँ, यक्ष्मन् यानी क्षय रोग से ग्रस्त घी में द्रवित करके चाटे।
english: Pills should be made from pathyā (chebulic myrobalan) and trivṛt (turpeth), accompanied by honey and juice. Those dry pills, of the measure of a māṣa, one with yakṣman (a wasting disease, usually equated with tuberculosis) should lick, melted in ghee.

words.gloss: pathyā (chebulic myrobalan), trivṛt (turpeth), pungent, hot water
steeped in snuk-milk (snuk, a spurge, probably Euphorbia neriifolia: probable)
in the powder of pathyā (chebulic myrobalan)

hindi: पथ्या यानी हरड़, त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ, कटु और गरम जल सर्वत्र इष्ट विरेचन है। पथ्या यानी हरड़ का चूर्ण स्नुक् यानी थूहर के क्षीर से भावित हो जाने पर मोदक बनाए।

words.gloss: of kola-seed measure (kola: jujube fruit, Ziziphus jujuba: probable)
of one with gulma (abdominal lump), belly (udara), liver (yakṛt), spleen (plīha), pain (śūla), ānāha (abdominal distension with retention), obstruction (vibandha, constipation)

hindi: कोल यानी बेर की गुठली के माप वाले और सूखे मोदकों को ताज़े मक्खन के साथ चटाए। गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, उदर, यकृत् यानी जिगर, प्लीहा यानी तिल्ली, शूल यानी पीड़ा, आनाह यानी पेट का फूलना और मल-वायु का रुकना, और विबन्ध यानी मलावरोध वाले का,
english: One should make (him) lick the balls, of the size of a kola (jujube) seed and dry, with fresh butter. of one with gulma (abdominal lump), belly (udara), liver, spleen, pain (śūla), ānāha (tying-up; distension of the abdomen with retention of stool and wind) and obstruction (vibandha),

line 05.02.177: 'modakān' is carried over from the previous unit. kola is kept as a fruit name. lehayet is the causative of √lih; glossary OPEN: literal 'should make (him) lick'. ENRICHMENT: kola = jujube fruit, Ziziphus jujuba (probable; kola is also a small-jujube name).

words.gloss: with eraṇḍa oil (castor oil, Ricinus communis: standard)
joined with kuṣṭha (costus root, Saussurea lappa: standard) and trikaṭuka (the three pungents: dried ginger, long pepper, black pepper)

hindi: कुष्ठ यानी कूठ और त्रिकटुक यानी सोंठ, पीपर और काली मिर्च से युक्त को एरण्ड यानी अरंडी के तैल के साथ चाटे। और ऊपर से सुखद जल पीए; यह विरेचन सुखकर है।
english: One should lick it, joined with kuṣṭha (costus root) and the trikaṭuka (the three pungents: dried ginger, long pepper, black pepper), with eraṇḍa (castor) oil. And one should drink pleasant water after; this purgative is easy.
notes:
line 05.02.179: The object ('it') is not named; 'etat' of the next unit refers back. kuṣṭha and eraṇḍa are kept as drug names. ENRICHMENT: eraṇḍa = Ricinus communis, castor (standard); kuṣṭha as a drug = Saussurea lappa (costus), standard (the word also names a skin disease; here it is a drug in a list); trikaṭuka = śuṇṭhī, pippalī, marica (standard).
